headline: Q2FY27 in the model: BUY with low conviction, the multiple does the work
summary: Dixon Technologies is an electronics manufacturing services company whose largest business is contract manufacturing of mobile phones. The Q2FY27 results filed with NSE on 30-Oct-2026 are now in the model data: revenue rose 46.7% YoY to Rs 21,794 crore, while profit to owners fell 48.7% YoY to Rs 343.7 crore because Q2FY26 included an estimated one-off other-income gain of Rs 387.9 crore; excluding one-offs, profit fell 3.7% YoY. The model target of Rs 17,376 implies 58.0% upside and blends relative P/E (Rs 19,250) with the consensus of 27 analysts (Rs 14,877); the DCF value of Rs 970.6 is excluded but points the other way, so conviction is Low. Analyst view: the relative value assumes both 40% earnings growth (the model cap) and a P/E of 69.9x against 55.9x today, and the target is 16.8% above the consensus mean; with profit excluding one-offs flat YoY on 47% revenue growth, we would treat the BUY as low conviction until margins stop falling.
highlights: Q2FY27 revenue of Rs 21,794 crore, up 46.7% YoY and 40.2% QoQ (NSE results filing, 30-Oct-2026).
Q2FY27 EBITDA excluding other income of Rs 596.8 crore, a margin of about 2.7% against about 3.8% in Q2FY26 (Rs 561.3 crore on Rs 14,855 crore).

Q2FY27 profit of Rs 410.9 crore including minority interest and Rs 343.7 crore to owners. This reconciles the two press figures: Rs 411 crore (Free Press Journal) is total profit and Rs 344 crore (The Hawk) is profit to owners.
Q1FY27 reported profit of Rs 663.4 crore included an estimated one-off gain of Rs 420.5 crore before tax from other income of Rs 528.3 crore; excluding it, profit was Rs 316.8 crore.
Shareholding on 30-Sep-2026: promoter 28.50% (28.92% a year earlier), FII 18.96%, DII 28.71% including mutual funds 19.26%; no promoter shares pledged (NSE shareholding pattern).
catalysts: Q3FY27 results, due by 14-Feb-2027 under SEBI LODR; the test is whether EBITDA margin recovers from about 2.7%.
A close back above the 200-day average, 8.9% above the current price, would reverse the current downtrend signal.
risks: Analyst view: the target depends on a re-rating. At the current P/E of 55.9x and trailing EPS of Rs 196.8, the bear case is Rs 10,472 (4.8% below the price) and the relative base case Rs 19,250 needs both 40% EPS growth and a 69.9x multiple.
Valuation cross-check: the DCF gives Rs 970.6 because free cash flow was only 0.47x of net profit over the base years. The price assumes cash generation the company has not yet shown.

Analyst view: the annual table shows FY26 one-offs of Rs 704.0 crore from the data source, more than the Rs 387.9 crore identified in the filed FY26 quarters, so FY26 EPS excluding one-offs (Rs 143.8) may be understated and the FY-end P/E history overstated.
Source inconsistency: balance-sheet equity implies book value of Rs 764.5 per share, against Rs 1,154 reported by the source. Return ratios should be checked against the annual report.
Market risk: the price is 16.8% below the 50-day average, RSI is 25.8, the stock fell as much as 38.4% in a year and underperformed the Nifty 50 by 18.7% over 12 months.

sources.title: Dixon Technologies Q2 FY27 profit falls 45% to Rs 411 crore, revenue jumps 47% to Rs 21,794 crore (Free Press Journal)
